questions.title: Designing, Representing, and Testing a Modular Login Subroutine (Q22, ITE 2016)

items.text:
A Login subroutine is under development as part of a larger program. Some of the requirements for this Login subroutine are as follows:

1. The usernames and passwords are stored in a sequential text file.

2. LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile will read the text file and places the usernames and passwords in an array of records.

3. FindUserNameAndPassword conducts a linear search of the array of records until the username is found and then checks if the password is correct for that username.

Consider the following algorithm for the Login subroutine.

BEGIN Login

valid = False

LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile

Get username from User

WHILE username is not equal to 9999 AND valid = False

Get password from User

found = False

FindUserNameAndPassword(username, password, found)

IF found = True THEN

PRINT “Valid details entered”

valid = True

ELSE

PRINT “Please try again”

Get username from User

 END IF

END WHILE

END Login
Explain the purpose of valid and found in the above algorithm.

criteria.criterion: Explains the purpose of both variables showing an understanding of their use in the subroutine
Identifies the purpose of a variable

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Valid is used as a flag to determine when the username and password has been entered correctly and to stop the program from asking the user to enter their username and password again.

Found is used to determine if the username entered by the user is located in the array of records and whether the password entered by the user matches the stored password for that username. It is initially set to False and then findUserNameAndPassword sets it to True if the username is found and the password matches.

criteria.criterion: Draws a correct structure chart
Draws a structure chart showing some understanding of the program
Shows an understanding of structure charts

items.text: The Login algorithm has been coded, however the subroutines called by Login are yet to be written. Describe how the Login code could be tested without these subroutines.

criteria.criterion: Shows an understanding of the use of stubs in this program
Shows an understanding of program development techniques

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
FindUserNameAndPassword and LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile could be replaced with stubs. For example, FindUserNameAndPassword could be coded as:

BEGIN FindUserNameAndPassword(username, password, found)

found = True

END FindUserNameAndPassword

LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile could be replaced with a stub which manually sets the contents of the array of records with some sample usernames and passwords, for example:

BEGIN LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile

arrUsers(1).username = “john”

arrUsers(1).password = “123456”

arrUsers(2).username = “fred”

arrUsers(2).password = “password”

END LoadUserNameAndPasswordFile

This would allow the main Login subroutine to be tested because the array of records will be populated and FindUserNameAndPassword will always return a value.

questions.title: Compare a linear search with a binary search of an array. (Q25, CSSA 2023)

items.text: Compare a linear search with a binary search of an array.

criteria.criterion: Compares a linear search with a binary search
Describes a linear and binary search
Describes a linear OR a binary search

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
A linear search accepts a target value and checks every element of the array to be searched in turn, until either a match is found or the end of the array is reached. If a match is found, the position of the match is reported, otherwise a message is written telling the user that the target is not present in the data.

A binary search is used on a sorted array to find a required element more quickly than using a linear search. It divides the data set into two parts and determines in which part the element is to be found. That part of the array is again divided into two parts and a further decision is made as to which part may contain the target value. The process is continued until either the value is found or there are no more elements in the data set to be checked. If a match is found, the position of the match is reported, otherwise a message is written telling the user that the target is not present in the data

items.text:
Consider the following algorithm which calculates the average of a list of test scores.

x = 0

REPEAT 

IF c[i] < > “9999” THEN 

x = x + c[i] 

i = i + 1 

ENDIF

y = x / i

Outline how the coding of the algorithm can be improved so that it is easier to maintain.

criteria.criterion:
Explains with multiple reasons how the algorithm could be improved so that it is
easier to maintain

markingRubricContentItem.text:
The algorithm could improve by utilising the following intrinsic and internal documentation
techniques:


• Use meaningful variable names – for example y could be changed to “average” to better reflect
its purpose.
• Use indentation to make the code more readable. For example, using indentation on repetition
control structures allows you to easily see parts of the code that require to be repeated.
• Use comments in the code – this allows other programmers to see the purpose of sections of code
more easily.
• Use of white space to chunk sections of code to make it more readable. For example, logically
grouping the variables being initialised and having white space after these.

questions.title: Developing and Testing an Algorithm to Validate Australian Tax File Numbers (Q27, CSSA 2014)

items.text:
The requirements for the validation of an Australian Tax File number (TFN) are as follows:

  • The number must be 9 digits long

  • A validity check procedure is applied wherein each digit of the TFN is multiplied against a given weight and the sum of these products must be a multiple of 11 (i.e. the remainder when the total is divided by 11 should equal 0).

  • The weights for each digit of the TFN are stored in the Weights array as follows:

Weights()

Index

1

2

3

4

5

6

7

8

9

Weight

1

4

3

7

5

8

6

9

10

 

  • The digits in each Tax File Number are also stored in an array TFN.

   eg.   A  TFN of 321 456 789 would be stored as follows

TFN()

Index

1

2

3

4

5

6

7

8

9

Digit

3

2

1

4

5

6

7

8

9

 

For example, a TFN of 321 456 789 would be validated like this:

Check length: Length of TFN = 9   Valid = True

Check sum:

3 x 1  = 3
2 x 4  = 8
1 x 3  = 3
4 x 7  = 28
5 x 5  = 25
6 x 8  = 48
7 x 6  = 42
8 x 9  = 72
9 x 10 = 90

The sum of 3+8+3+28+25+48+42+72+90 = 319

319 is a multiple of 11 (319/11 = 29, no remainder). Valid = True

Output:  TFN VALID True

 

Consider the following TFN_Check algorithm, which is designed to carry out the TFN validity check for possible inputted TFN numbers.

The output of the algorithm should be either: TFN IS VALID  True   or    TFN IS VALID False

 

BEGIN TFN_Check (TFN(), WEIGHTS())

TOTAL = 0

VALID = False

IF the length of TFN = 9 THEN

VALID = True

END IF

 

FOR n = 1 TO 9

TOTAL = TOTAL + TFN(n) * WEIGHTS(n)

IF TOTAL = The reminder of TOTAL divided by 11 is not equal to 0 THEN

VALID = False

ELSE

VALID = True

ENDIF

NEXT

PRINT ‘TFN IS VALID?’, VALID

END TFN_Check
This algorithm has errors. Re-write the algorithm so it correctly validates a Tax File Number.

criteria.criterion: Moves final IF statement out of the FOR loop AND includes initial check for TFN length
Moves final IF statement out of the FOR loop OR includes initial check for TFN length
Shows a minimal understanding by attempting a valid change

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
BEGIN TFN_CHECK
          Total = 0

          Valid = False

          IF the length of TFN = 9 THEN
               Valid = True
          ENDIF

          IF Valid THEN
               FOR n = 1 TO 9

                    Total = Total + TFN[n] * Weights[n]

               NEXT

               IF Total = The reminder of Total divided by 11 is not equal to 0 THEN
                    Valid = False
               ELSE
                    Valid = True
               ENDIF

          END IF
          PRINT ‘TFN IS VALID?’, Valid
     END

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Good aspects:

● Intrinsic naming of the function and all variables

● Comment includes the name of the author and date, so developers can contact them with any
questions

● There are no global variables relied on - it accepts a name and returns a Boolean

Poor aspects/modifications required

● The major issue with this algorithm is the hard-coding of the values 3 and 12, which makes it
only suitable for checking names of that desired length. It should accept three parameters:
inputName: String, minLength: integer and maxLength: integer. On the fourth line the condition
is then length(inputName) <=maxLength AND length(inputName) >= minLength This means
an example call would be checkNameLength(“Claudio”,3,12) which would return True.

● The opening comment should also include details about the purpose of the function.

items.text: Write an algorithm that calculates the total number of cups of coffee sold for the long weekend and the average number of cups sold per day across the weekend.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
BEGIN TotalCoffeesSold

BEGIN SaturdaySales

     DayNum = 1
